about.title: Ojai Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Ojai's small-town roads carry a mix of local traffic, weekend visitors headed toward Lake Casitas, and cyclists drawn to the valley's scenery, and that mix shows up in the collision counts along Route 150, Grand Avenue, Ojai Avenue, and Cuyama Road. Public records show 32 injury collisions and 42 injured people in the most recent reporting year, with reports clustering on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. — a pattern worth noting if you're piecing together how a crash happened. After a collision, the days that follow matter: insurers often move fast, sometimes asking for a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge you anything; we simply connect injured Ojai residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at the facts, protect evidence while it's still available, and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: Two-Year Clock Starts Now
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit, but it can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like Ventura County or Caltrans — is involved. An attorney can flag that deadline early so it doesn't quietly pass.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Zero You Out
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you're found partly responsible for the crash, though your share of fault reduces the amount. An attorney can help make sure your percentage of blame isn't overstated by the other driver's insurer.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case, and attorneys in our network work on contingency — meaning there's no fee unless you recover money.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's best to hold off. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later, and you're not required to give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer. Speaking with an attorney first can help you understand what, if anything, you should say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on Route 150 or Grand Avenue and involved a county road issue?
items.answer: Claims involving a government-maintained road, like a stretch of Route 150 or a county intersection, can carry a much shorter filing deadline — sometimes just six months. It's important to have someone look at the specifics of where and how the crash occurred as soon as possible.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with one.
